items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: Joe was pretty clever. And he liked to hear everybody in the band. No one person, no. He wanted to hear everybody blended. He was a good leader.

ctx.x: Who did the arrangements for that first band?

That first album? Oh, I don't know. Let's see. He had, well, mostly, we had stock arrangements and just a little skeleton move. Mm-hmm. Just to keep you together, you know. Mm-hmm. Big Randy like now. Mm-hmm. But he liked his music. Joe was pretty clever. And he liked to hear everybody in the band. No one person, no. He wanted to hear everybody blended. He was a good leader. items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: And spent a year or so at Anderson until King Oliver sent for us to come to Chicago. And stayed with them, with King Oliver until 1926, August.

ctx.x: Can you tell us something about your training and taking lessons and so on?

Well, I started taking lessons around 9 years of age with my uncle, Wooden Joe Nicholas. He was my big influence on this jazz scene. And later on, I went to Papa Teo and took lessons with him for about a couple of years. Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915. Then I started to go pro. My first gigs around New Orleans was with the Maple Leaf Band. Then Buddy Petite's Band. When Jimmy Noon left to go to Chicago, I played with Buddy Petite and several other bands around New Orleans.…
